title: The Length of a Benefit Period on a Healthy Options Card Coming Into Use
content:
For the purpose of the allowance made available as a Ridgecrest Healthy Options Card comes into use, the length of a benefit period is taken from the basis the card's allowance is loaded on and from when the programme opened.

**The rule.** A benefit period is taken to have three months, where the card's allowance is loaded on calendar quarters of the benefit year and the programme opened within the benefit year; it is taken to have twelve months, where the card's allowance is made available once a year and the programme opened within the benefit year; and it is taken to have one month in every other case.

| The card's loading basis | The programme opened | Months in a benefit period |
|---|---|---|
| calendar quarters of the benefit year | within the benefit year | 3 |
| once a year | within the benefit year | 12 |
| any other case | — | 1 |

A programme opened within the benefit year is one whose opening day falls no later than the day the reckoning is made, the months from the opening day to that day being not fewer than none.

**A point of judgement.** The first two rows are distinguished by the card's loading basis alone: a card loaded on calendar quarters takes 3 months to a benefit period; a card whose allowance is made available once a year takes 12. Every other card, a card loaded on calendar months among them, takes 1 month to a benefit period.
